chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abd Allah ibn Salih al-Khash'ami, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about pain in the loins. He said: 'Adopt what falls from the food-spread and eat it.' I said: 'So I did that, and it went away from me.' Ibrahim said: 'I had found that in the right side and the left, so I took that (eating the fallen crumbs), and I benefited by it.'

key_terms.الْخَاصِرَةِ: Pain in the loins or lower back

ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic remedy for loins pain mentioned in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical wisdom of utilizing food scraps as a medicinal remedy, reflecting the Shia tradition of valuing both spiritual and physical well-being through prophetic practices. The narration underscores the efficacy of simple, everyday actions in healing, with the narrator Ibrahim noting the specific benefit for both the right and left sides of the body, suggesting a holistic approach to physical ailments.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Abdullah Bin Salih Al Khash’amy who said,

‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> of the waist pain. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon you is with what falls from the food-spread, so eat it’. So I did that, so it went away from me’. 
Ibrahim (the narrator) said, ‘I had found that in the right side and the left, so I took with that (eating the fallen crumbs), so I benefited by it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from ‘Abd Allah ibn Salih al- Khath’amiy who has said the following:

“I once complained before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, against lower back pain. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must eat pieces of food that fall on the table-spread.’ I (the narrator) followed the instruction and the pain went away. Ibrahim has said, ‘I then found it on the left and the right side; I did the same thing again and benefited thereby.’”
